First, let's sketch the graph of  $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{4})+\pi :$   

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14252450/assets/42eb38a11d9d63e05c0078bae4c052566b3162571e8563f22cd52ae31bc6dbd7.png)

The domain of   $\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{4})+\pi $ is $(-\infty ,\infty ).$  

Now, substituting $x=4$ directly into the limit, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{4})+\pi ) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1)+\pi ) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+\pi ) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{4}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
